q: Qiyaamah has drawn close and the moon has been split
(by Rasulullaah ﷺ in Makkah when the Mushrikeen requested him to perform this miracle).
v.s: The Hour has come near, and the moon has split [in two].
v.c: The Hour has drawn near and the moon was split ˹in two˺.

q: (However, the Mushrikeen are so stubborn that even)
they turn away and say that it is magic that will soon vanish.
v.s: And if they see a sign [i.e., miracle], they turn away and say, "Passing magic."
v.c: Yet, whenever they see a sign, they turn away, saying, “Same old magic!”

q: (the truth will always remain the truth and falsehood will always remain falsehood regardless of what people have to say).
v.s: And they denied and followed their inclinations. But for every matter is a [time of] settlement.
v.c: They rejected ˹the truth˺ and followed their own desires—and every matter will be settled—

q: has come to them in which there is sufficient warning to caution
v.s: And there has already come to them of information that in which there is deterrence.
v.c: even though the stories ˹of destroyed nations˺ that have already come to them are a sufficient deterrent.

q: (them because they refuse to believe the Ambiyaa ﵊)?
v.s: Extensive wisdom - but warning does not avail [them].
v.c: ˹This Quran is˺ profound ˹in˺ wisdom, but warnings are of no benefit ˹to them˺.

q: (because they will have to learn the error of their ways the hard way when Allaah's punishment or Qiyaamah arrives). (The Day of Qiyaamah will be)
(for those guilty of kufr and sin).
v.s: So leave them, [O Muhammad]. The Day the Caller calls to something forbidding,
v.c: So turn away from them ˹O Prophet˺. ˹And wait for˺ the Day ˹when˺ the caller will summon ˹them˺ for something horrifying.

q: Their gazes will be cast down
(because of worry and shame for their past)
and they shall emerge from their graves
as if they are scattered locusts...
v.s: Their eyes humbled, they will emerge from the graves as if they were locusts spreading,
v.c: With eyes downcast, they will come forth from the graves as if they were swarming locusts,

q: (towards the Plain of Reckoning where they will be called to account for their actions).
The Kaafiroon will say, “This is an extremely difficult day.”
v.s: Racing ahead toward the Caller. The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult Day."
v.c: rushing towards the caller. The disbelievers will cry, “This is a difficult Day!”

q: and said that he was a madman and he was rebuked
v.s: The people of Noah denied before them, and they denied Our servant and said, "A madman," and he was repelled.
v.c: Before them, the people of Noah denied ˹the truth˺ and rejected Our servant, calling ˹him˺ insane. And he was intimidated.

q: So he made du'aa to his Rabb
“Indeed I am overpowered so assist me
(avenge my cause and destroy them, leaving no Kaafir alive).'
v.s: So he invoked his Lord, "Indeed, I am overpowered, so help."
v.c: So he cried out to his Lord, “I am helpless, so help ˹me˺!”

q: We opened up the doors of the sky to
v.s: Then We opened the gates of the heaven with rain pouring down
v.c: So We opened the gates of the sky with pouring rain,

q: (in addition to the waters from the sky)
We opened springs in the earth
(raining from the sky and gushing from the earth)
(resulting in a flood as punishment for them).
v.s: And caused the earth to burst with springs, and the waters met for a matter already predestined.
v.c: and caused the earth to burst with springs, so the waters met for a fate already set.

q: on an ark of planks and nails
v.s: And We carried him on a [construction of] planks and nails,
v.c: We carried him on that ˹Ark made˺ of planks and nails,

q: This was the reward for the one
v.s: Sailing under Our observation as reward for he who had been denied.
v.c: sailing under Our ˹watchful˺ Eyes—a ˹fair˺ punishment on behalf of the one ˹they˺ denied.

q: so is there anyone who will take heed
v.s: And We left it as a sign, so is there any who will remember?
v.c: We certainly left this as a sign. So is there anyone who will be mindful?

q: was My punishment and My warnings?
v.s: And how [severe] were My punishment and warning.
v.c: Then how ˹dreadful˺ were My punishment and warnings!

q: Undoubtedly We have made the Qur'aan simple to take lesson from
so is there any who will take lessons?
v.s: And We have certainly made the Qur’ān easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
v.c: And We have certainly made the Quran easy to remember. So is there anyone who will be mindful?

q: (the message of Towheed that their Nabi Hood ﵊ brought to them),
v.s: ʿAad denied; and how [severe] were My punishment and warning.
v.c: ’Ȃd ˹also˺ rejected ˹the truth˺. Then how ˹dreadful˺ were My punishment and warnings!

q: Verily We sent against them a furious wind during
v.s: Indeed, We sent upon them a screaming wind on a day of continuous misfortune,
v.c: Indeed, We sent against them a furious wind, on a day of unrelenting misery,

q: (and left them lying dead on the ground)
as if they were uprooted palm trunks.
v.s: Extracting the people as if they were trunks of palm trees uprooted.
v.c: that snatched people up, leaving them like trunks of uprooted palm trees.

v.s: And how [severe] were My punishment and warning.
v.c: Then how ˹dreadful˺ were My punishment and warnings!

q: Undoubtedly We have made the Qur'aan simple from which to take lesson
so is there any who will take lessons?
v.s: And We have certainly made the Qur’ān easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
v.c: And We have certainly made the Quran easy to remember. So is there anyone who will be mindful? The People of Ṣâliḥ

q: (the Ambiyaa ﵊). (By rejecting the message of their Nabi Saalih ﵊, they actually rejected the message of all the Ambiyaa ﵊ because every Nabi brought the same message.)
v.s: Thamūd denied the warning.
v.c: Thamûd rejected the warnings ˹as well˺,

q: They said, “If we were to follow a single solitary human
from among ourselves, we would surely be in error and insane.”
v.s: And said, "Is it one human being among us that we should follow? Indeed, we would then be in error and madness.
v.c: arguing, “How can we follow one ˹average˺ human being from among us? We would then truly be misguided and insane.

q: come only to him from among all of us
(instead of coming to one of our affluent people)?
he is but an arrogant liar.”
v.s: Has the message been sent down upon him from among us? Rather, he is an insolent liar."
v.c: Has the revelation been sent down ˹only˺ to him out of ˹all of˺ us? In fact, he is a boastful liar.”

q: they shall come to know who is an arrogant liar.
(They will soon learn that it was they and not the Nabi who was “an arrogant liar”).
v.s: They will know tomorrow who is the insolent liar.
v.c: ˹It was revealed to Ṣâliḥ,˺ “They will soon know who the boastful liar is.

q: (When the Thamud requested Saalih ﵊ to bring a pregnant camel from a rock, he made du'aa to Allaah Who said to him,)
camel as a test to them
(to see which of them will then believe that you are a Nabi and who will not)
so watch them and be patient.”
v.s: Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as trial for them, so watch them and be patient.
v.c: We are sending the she-camel as a test for them. So watch them ˹closely˺, and have patience.

q: (between the miraculous camel and the rest of their livestock)
and each should present himself on his turn

(the she camel having a day for herself and the rest of their livestock having the next day for themselves).” (However, the people were dissatisfied with this arrangement and decided to have her killed.)
v.s: And inform them that the water is shared between them, each [day of] drink attended [by turn].
v.c: And tell them that the ˹drinking˺ water must be divided between them ˹and her˺, each taking a turn to drink ˹every other day˺.”

v.s: But they called their companion, and he dared and hamstrung [her].
v.c: But they roused a companion of theirs, so he dared to kill ˹her˺.

v.s: And how [severe] were My punishment and warning.
v.c: Then how ˹dreadful˺ were My punishment and warnings!

q: Verily We sent against them a single shout
(a deafening blast from the sky, which killed them all)
and they became like the rubble dry sticks
(that are thrown away by one who builds enclosures for cattle) (This is a proverb the Arabs used to refer to something completely destroyed and useless).
v.s: Indeed, We sent upon them one shriek [i.e., blast from the sky], and they became like the dry twig fragments of an [animal] pen.
v.c: Indeed, We sent against them ˹only˺ one ˹mighty˺ blast, leaving them like the twigs of fence-builders.

q: Undoubtedly We have made the Qur'aan simple to take lesson from
so is there any who will take lessons?
v.s: And We have certainly made the Qur’ān easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
v.c: And We have certainly made the Quran easy to remember. So is there anyone who will be mindful?

q: The people of Loot rejected the warners
v.s: The people of Lot denied the warning.
v.c: The people of Lot ˹also˺ rejected the warnings.

q: Verily We sent against them a powerful wind
that showered stones on them, except for the family of Loot ﵊ whom We rescued during the close
of the last hour of the night.
v.s: Indeed, We sent upon them a storm of stones, except the family of Lot - We saved them before dawn.
v.c: We unleashed upon them a storm of stones. As for ˹the believers of˺ Lot’s family, We delivered them before dawn

q: (to the Mu'mineen because of their Imaan).
do We reward the grateful ones.
v.s: As favor from Us. Thus do We reward he who is grateful.
v.c: as a blessing from Us. This is how We reward whoever gives thanks.

q: certainly warned them that We would seize
v.s: And he had already warned them of Our assault, but they disputed the warning.
v.c: He had already warned them of Our ˹crushing˺ blow but they disputed the warnings.

q: (When Allaah sent some angels as guests to Loot ﵊ to inform him about impending the punishment.)
(blinded them as they tried). (As this happened, they were told,)
v.s: And they had demanded from him his guests, but We obliterated their eyes, [saying], "Taste My punishment and warning."
v.c: And they even demanded his angel-guests from him, so We blinded their eyes. ˹And they were told,˺ “Taste then My punishment and warnings!”

q: Without a doubt, during the early hours of the morning a punishment with long- lasting effects afflicted them.
(Stones were rained on them and their cities were lifted to the sky and flung upside down.)
v.s: And there came upon them by morning an abiding punishment.
v.c: And indeed, by the early morning they were overwhelmed by an unrelenting torment.

v.s: So taste My punishment and warning.
v.c: ˹Again they were told,˺ “Taste now My punishment and warnings!”

q: Undoubtedly We have made the Qur'aan simple to take lesson from, so is there! any who will take lessons?
v.s: And We have certainly made the Qur’ān easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
v.c: And We have certainly made the Quran easy to remember. So is there anyone who will be mindful?

q: definitely came to the people of Fir'oun.
v.s: And there certainly came to the people of Pharaoh warning.
v.c: And indeed, the warnings ˹also˺ came to the people of Pharaoh.

q: They rejected every one of Our
them with the grasp of One Who is Most Mighty and Powerful
v.s: They denied Our signs, all of them, so We seized them with a seizure of one Exalted in Might and Perfect in Ability.
v.c: ˹But˺ they rejected all of Our signs, so We seized them with the ˹crushing˺ grip of the Almighty, Most Powerful.

q: (of the past, which makes them think that they will not be punished)
v.s: Are your disbelievers better than those [former ones], or have you immunity in the scriptures?
v.c: Now, are you ˹Meccan˺ disbelievers superior to those ˹destroyed peoples˺? Or have you ˹been granted˺ immunity ˹from punishment˺ in divine Books?

q: (who can defend ourselves against Allaah's punishment).”
v.s: Or do they say, "We are an assembly supporting [each other]"?
v.c: Or do they say, “We are all ˹a˺ united ˹front˺, bound to prevail.”?

q: The band shall soon be defeated
and they will turn their backs and flee
(as the Kuffaar did in the Battles of Badr and Ahzaab).
v.s: [Their] assembly will be defeated, and they will turn their backs [in retreat].
v.c: ˹Soon˺ their united front will be defeated and ˹forced to˺ flee.

q: The fact is that Qiyaamah is their appointment
and Qiyaamah shall be most severe and most bitter
v.s: But the Hour is their appointment [for due punishment], and the Hour is more disastrous and more bitter.
v.c: Better yet, the Hour is their appointed time—and the Hour will be most catastrophic and most bitter.

v.s: Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness..
v.c: Indeed, the wicked are ˹entrenched˺ in misguidance, and ˹are bound for˺ blazes.

q: The day when they shall be dragged into the Fire
(and it will be said to them)
v.s: The Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces [it will be said], "Taste the touch of Saqar."
v.c: On the Day they will be dragged into the Fire on their faces, ˹they will be told,˺ “Taste the touch of Hell!”

q: We have certainly created everything by
(so that everything fulfils the requirements for its task and so that everything happens when it is destined to happen).
v.s: Indeed, all things We created with predestination.
v.c: Indeed, We have created everything, perfectly preordained.

q: (when We desire to make something happen)
is but once like the blinking of an eye.
v.s: And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye.
v.c: Our command is but a single word, done in the blink of an eye.

q: (in the past and can do the same to you if you choose to reject Imaan)
so is there any who will take heed
(mend his ways and turn to Allaah)?
v.s: And We have already destroyed your kinds, so is there any who will remember?
v.c: We have already destroyed the likes of you. So will any ˹of you˺ be mindful?

q: (in the records of their actions so that nothing was omitted).
v.s: And everything they did is in written records.
v.c: Everything they have done is ˹listed˺ in ˹their˺ records.

q: Every minor and major act is recorded
(so a person cannot hope to escape punishment based on insufficient evidence against him).
v.s: And every small and great [thing] is inscribed.
v.c: Every matter, small and large, is written ˹precisely˺.

q: Verily those with Taqwa shall be
v.s: Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and rivers,
v.c: Indeed, the righteous will be amid Gardens and rivers,

v.s: In a seat of honour near a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability.
v.c: at the Seat of Honour in the presence of the Most Powerful Sovereign.
